request.current_synthesis: M1 completed the planned candidate-free plant and branch measurement. Observed facts: the loaded simulator uses a 0.002 s integration step, 10-step action hold (0.020 s), integrator code 0, explicit derived body masses and inertias, 0.5 joint damping, 0.01 armature, and 5:1 actuator gear. The 256-entry branch catalog has near-zero forward-kinematic residuals, but exact geometric solutions often violate the +/-170 degree joint limits: for example, at radius 0.06 m and target angle -180 degrees the open branch has -66.25 degrees minimum margin while the folded branch has +19.93 degrees; at radius 0.20 m and angle +157.5 degrees the folded branch has -9.83 degrees while the open branch has +34.83 degrees. Thus the initial model's claim that the annulus has multiple physical solutions is geometrically supported but its implication that both branches are feasible across the annulus is contradicted; at least one branch must be selected with limit awareness, while reachability itself is not disproven. The pulse trials support the hold-dynamics concern: one full-control-period pulse followed by zero control produced 31.7 mm post-pulse end-effector travel from the straight reset, 28.7 mm at a 0.20 m target configuration, and 8.35 mm at representative 0.06 m configurations, with peak end-effector speeds up to 1.19 m/s. These excursions are comparable to or larger than the 10 mm tolerance, so braking and low-velocity regulation remain a credible dominant mechanism. M1 therefore supports continuing a combined route: train and measure over the full official annulus while explicitly diagnosing branch validity, limit margin, first-entry velocity, settling, and hold interruptions. M1 does not reveal which mechanism dominates learned-policy failures because no policy was exercised, and its local pulse response does not establish protected-evaluator semantics.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved distinction is whether a memoryless policy trained on the full official geometry can learn adequate branch selection and braking from the existing observation and reward, or whether the 98% goal requires an explicit control/temporal capability change. Findings that would change the route are: failures concentrated before valid branch approach or at negative limit margins would prioritize branch-aware trajectory management; fast first entry followed by late interruptions with high residual velocity would prioritize stabilization and temporal/control shaping; broad success on both diagnostics but poor inner-annulus coverage would prioritize the training distribution; and evidence that failures depend on hidden hold progress would justify temporal memory. M1 makes branch-limit awareness and stabilization decision-relevant but cannot rank them without policy trajectories.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete a 2 second uninterrupted 1 cm hold. The startup decision therefore must identify whether the first policy route should prioritize braking and local stabilization, branch and joint-limit management, or both.
